extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, poets, and educated readers interested in poetic criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing poetry and literary criticism: how to judge poets and poems, what counts as valuable criticism, and which poetical/prose qualities to prize. Emphasizes context, characteristic qualities, and the critic's proper aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge by characteristic qualities, not isolated failures
rubrics_metrics.description: I know nothing that surpasses the vileness of deciding on the merits of a poet or painter — not by characteristic defects, for where there is genius, these always point to his characteristic beauties — but by accidental failures or faulty passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let accidental or isolated bad lines determine an artist's whole reputation. Example anti-patterns: ridiculing incidental props ("knitting-needles and broom-twigs") or quoting single faulty passages as representative of the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism should elucidate beauties, not merely note defects
rubrics_metrics.description: He who points out and elucidates the beauties of an original work, does indeed give me interesting information; he who tells me that there are defects tells me nothing which I should not have taken for granted without his information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus reviews on explaining and illustrating the work's merits in a way that gives readers new insight. Merely cataloguing defects is uninformative and of limited value to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid arrogant imposition of fixed canons
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are conducted... the reviewers support their decisions by reference to fixed canons of criticism, previously established and deduced from the nature of man; reflecting minds will pronounce it arrogance in them thus to announce themselves to men of letters as the guides of their taste and judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about asserting rigid, universal rules as if they settle taste. Critics should be reflective rather than prescriptive and avoid claiming absolute authority over readers' judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not magnify trivial faults by reprinting them as representative
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in a volume of poetry, the critic should find a poem or passage which he deems more especially worthless, he is sure to select and reprint it in the review; by which, on his own grounds, he wastes as much more paper than the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the practice of selecting and amplifying a few poor passages (e.g., doggerel or lapses) and presenting them as typical. This misleads the public and distorts the author's overall achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate works in context; consider author's intentions and reader's background
rubrics_metrics.description: A careful and repeated examination of these [Lyrical Ballads] confirms me in the belief, that the omission of less than a hundred lines would have precluded nine-tenths of the criticism on this work... provided they were perused without knowledge of, or reference to, the author's peculiar opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how prior knowledge of an author's theory or opinions colors reception. Judge passages in the context of the whole work and the intended audience; what offends when framed as deliberate may be read as inattention when decontextualized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat living and dead authors by the same standard
rubrics_metrics.description: "Why should we judge by a different rule two printed works only because the one author is alive and the other in his grave?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply different critical rules merely because an author is living. Evaluate printed works on their merits consistently regardless of the author's living status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the whole work; minor inferior pieces are not decisive
rubrics_metrics.description: It is hard and unjust to fix the attention on a few separate and insulated poems with as much aversion as if they had been so many plague-spots on the whole work... the poems, therefore, at the worst, could only be regarded as so many light or inferior coins in a rouleau of gold, not as so much alloy in a weight of bullion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appraising a collection, weigh minor or lesser pieces proportionately to the whole; a few trifles should not overturn the value of the larger work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that defects may indicate characteristic beauties
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is genius, [defects] always point to his characteristic beauties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use apparent faults as clues to an author's distinctive powers; characteristic failures can reveal the boldness or novelty underlying an artist's strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of excellent poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of superior poetic qualities: 'greater splendour, a deeper pathos, profounder reflections, and a more sustained dignity of language and of metre' — invention, pictorial richness, variety of species, and the capacity to combine wisdom with wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating poetry, consider these formal and substantive virtues: grandeur, emotional depth, philosophical or reflective substance, dignity of diction and versification, inventive imagery, and versatility across poetic forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of excellent prose and essays
rubrics_metrics.description: His prose is always intelligible and always entertaining... in a style so lively and poignant, yet so uniformly classical and perspicuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For prose criticism and essays, prize clarity, liveliness, classical balance, perspicuity, and the ability to convey information with engaging style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial character and industry as evaluative factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet's matchless industry and perseverance in his pursuits; the regular and methodical tenor of his daily labours... punctual in trifles, steadfast in the performance of highest duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider an author's sustained industry, consistency, and moral character as part of their overall reputation and as contextual evidence of their seriousness and reliability as a writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious of public influence and critics' motives
rubrics_metrics.description: The multitudinous public... the nominal despot on the throne of criticism... reviews written from humour or interest, from enmity or arrogance, and to abide the decision 'of him that reads in malice, or him that reads after dinner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should be aware of the crowd's influence and suspect that reviewers may be motivated by whim, interest, or malice; maintain independent, reasoned judgment rather than echoing public clamor.
